conceptual assets.information: The configuration consists of protected-region address bounds, matching modes, and read, write, and execute permissions on which PMP access enforcement depends. It is written through the CSR interface and returned through CSR read-back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Unauthorized CSR writes can modify region bounds, modes, and permissions through the writes at lines 113-145 and 157-178; those settings determine whether accesses fault and can therefore block required accesses through lines 285-354.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could issue unauthorized CSR writes to alter a region or permission so protected accesses are permitted or required accesses are rejected.

conceptual assets.information: The per-region lock bits determine whether the associated PMP configuration and address can be changed. The state controls the immutability of the protection policy after configuration.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: A CSR write can set the lock bit at line 145, while the lock gates later configuration and address writes at lines 127 and 170; setting or corrupting it can both weaken policy integrity and prevent required reconfiguration.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could set or corrupt a lock bit to freeze an incorrect policy or alter the lock state before changing protected-region settings.

conceptual assets.information: The current instruction or load/store address selected for checking is the address whose region membership and permissions determine the access result. It is consumed by internal comparisons rather than returned as an address.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The address can reveal code or data access patterns through the address-dependent fault status at lines 285, 295-296, and 351-363; the selection at line 244 can substitute the checked address based on the operation mode, and the selected address controls whether the access is faulted and blocked.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe fault responses to infer protected access locations or steer the address-selection inputs so a different address is checked and the intended access is denied or misclassified.

conceptual assets.information: This internal decision identifies which PMP region applies to the current access. No port carries the selected-region result directly; it is computed internally and used to select the applicable policy.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The match logic selects the governing region from address comparisons and PMP modes at lines 303-312, and corruption of that selection can apply the wrong policy or propagate through line 354 to block the access.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could corrupt the region-match decision or its inputs so an access uses a permissive region or is falsely treated as unmatched and faulted.

conceptual assets.concept: PMP access permission and fault verdict
conceptual assets.information: The verdict is the internally combined decision that the current access is allowed or should fault. It is registered and exposed as the fault status used by the surrounding processor.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The combined failure decision drives the registered fault output at lines 351-363, so altering the verdict can create false faults or suppress required faults; the debug condition at line 363 can suppress the fault in normal protection operation and thereby produce an incorrect security result.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could corrupt the fail or fault path, or assert the debug input, to turn denied accesses into allowed ones or generate spurious faults that stop execution.

considered, not kept.reason: CSR address and write-enable fields only select whether and which configuration element is accessed, so the access-command-fields rule bars them as information of their own.
Clock and reset inputs and their reset paths are explicitly excluded from conceptual assets by the clock-and-reset rule.
